english.title: Occupier / manager of premises fail to keep controlled drugs in a locked store
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being

(A)_[the occupier]_
(B)_[a person concerned in the management]_

of

(C)_[premises occupied by a retail dealer for the purposes of his business]_
(D)_[premises occupied by a retail dealer for the purposes of her business]_
(E)_[a care home]_

at **(..SPECIFY LOCATION OF PREMISES..), failed to ensure that all controlled drugs on the premises were, so far as circumstances permit, kept in a locked safe, cabinet or room which was so constructed and maintained as to prevent unauthorised access to the drugs
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 3(2) and (3) of the Misuse of Drugs (Safe Custody) Regulations 1973 and section 18(1) of, and Schedule 4 to, the Misuse of Drugs Act 1971.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
occupier/person concerned in management of
premises occupied by a retail dealer for purposes of his/her business OR
a care home
failed to ensure controlled drugs on those premises
kept in a clocked safe/cabinet/room
constructed and maintained as to prevent unauthorised access

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) As per regulation 3(4), this offence is not committed in relation to controlled drugs that are for the time being under the direct supervision of a pharmacist (in respect of which no direction under section 12(2) of the Misuse of Drugs Act 1971 is in force), or in relation to a care home, the person in charge or a member of staff designated by him for the purpose.
(ii) As per regulation 4(1), this offence does not apply to a safe, cabinet or room in relation to which a certificate issued by the chief officer of police, under regulation 4(2), is in force.

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the prescribed sum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.Time limit for prosecutions:
None

Note:
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
